title: Content Delivery Networks (CDN)
intro: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) is a globally distributed network of Point of Presence (PoP) edge servers that caches assets close to end users.
objectives: Evaluate Anycast GeoDNS routing and BGP latency optimization.
Formulate cache invalidation strategies using surrogate keys and versioned URLs.
Leverage stale-while-revalidate and origin shielding to eliminate origin stampedes.
body:
### How CDNs Slash Latency
Transcontinental internet latency is bounded by the speed of light in fiber (~5ms per 1,000 km). Round-trips between Tokyo and Virginia take ~160ms. By caching static assets (images, JavaScript, CSS) and pre-rendered API responses at regional Edge PoPs, response times drop to < 15ms.

### Origin Shielding & Tiered Caching
When hundreds of regional PoPs miss simultaneously, the origin server faces a devastating stampede. An **Origin Shield** introduces an intermediate parent cache tier that consolidates regional edge misses, collapsing 100 origin queries into a single origin request.
keyIdea: The fastest request is the one that never hits your datacenter. Offload 90%+ of ingress traffic at the edge using Anycast and surrogate caching headers.

concepts.title: Anycast Routing
concepts.body: Multiple physical PoPs across the globe advertise the exact same IP address via BGP. Internet routers automatically route client packets to the topologically closest PoP.

concepts.title: Stale-While-Revalidate
concepts.body: Edge immediately returns cached stale data to the client while asynchronously fetching fresh content from the origin in the background.

examples: Cloudflare Edge caching dynamic responses with Cache-Tag invalidation.
Netflix Open Connect CDN appliances deployed directly inside ISP datacenters.

quiz.prompt: What does an Origin Shield protect against?
options: Cache misses across hundreds of regional PoPs swamping the primary backend database
quiz.explanation: An Origin Shield aggregates cache misses across edge PoPs so the primary origin receives only one consolidated fetch.
